options.name: Stripe CLI + launchd (macOS)
options.description: Run stripe listen locally 24/7 via launchd daemon. Stripe CLI forwards webhooks to a local script (e.g., Python/Node). Works only while Mac is awake and on same network. Not cloud-reliable.
options.reliability: Low - depends on Mac uptime, network, no failover. Not suitable for production.
options.setup:
1. Install Stripe CLI: brew install stripe/stripe-cli/stripe
2. Login: stripe login
3. Create launchd plist at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.stripe.webhook.plist:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>com.stripe.webhook</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
        <string>/usr/local/bin/stripe</string>
        <string>listen</string>
        <string>--forward-to</string>
        <string>http://localhost:3000/webhook</string>
        <string>--api-key</string>
        <string>sk_test_...</string>
    </array>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
    <key>KeepAlive</key>
    <true/>
    <key>StandardOutPath</key>
    <string>/tmp/stripe-webhook.log</string>
    <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
    <string>/tmp/stripe-webhook.err</string>
</dict>
</plist>
4. Load: launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.stripe.webhook.plist
5. Ensure local script (e.g., Node.js Express) listens on port 3000.
Note: Mac must stay awake; use caffeinate -dim to prevent sleep.

options.name: Cloudflare Workers (Free Tier)
options.description: Use Cloudflare Workers to receive Stripe webhooks via HTTP, process them, and optionally forward to a queue or storage. Free tier: 100k requests/day, 10ms CPU time per request. Must verify Stripe signature using Web Crypto API (no Node crypto).
options.cost: $0 (free tier up to 100k requests/day; $5/month for 10M requests)
options.reliability: High - global edge network, 99.99% uptime SLA, auto-scaling.

options.name: AWS Lambda + API Gateway
options.description: Serverless function behind API Gateway HTTP API. Free tier: 1M requests/month, 400k GB-seconds. Stripe webhooks POST to Lambda via API Gateway URL.
options.cost: $0 (free tier for low volume; ~$0.20/month for 100k requests after free tier)
options.reliability: Very High - AWS infrastructure, 99.99% SLA for API Gateway.

options.name: Vercel Functions (Hobby Tier)
options.description: Serverless functions on Vercel. Hobby tier: 100 GB-hours, 100k requests/month. Stripe webhooks POST to a serverless function (e.g., /api/webhook.js).
options.reliability: High - Vercel edge network, but cold starts can be slow. No SLA on free tier.

options.name: ngrok (Free Tier)
options.description: Expose local server via ngrok tunnel. Free tier: 1 random domain, 40 connections/minute, 8k bytes/sec. Not for production; only for testing.
options.reliability: Low - rate limited, ephemeral URLs, no SLA.
options.setup:
1. Install ngrok: brew install ngrok/ngrok/ngrok
2. Run local webhook handler (e.g., Node.js on port 3000).
3. Start tunnel: ngrok http 3000
4. Copy forwarding URL (e.g., https://abc123.ngrok.io) and set as Stripe webhook endpoint.
5. Keep terminal open; use tmux or launchd to persist.
Note: Free tier URL changes each restart; paid has reserved subdomain.

recommendation.cheapest: Cloudflare Workers Free Tier ($0) or AWS Lambda Free Tier ($0) - both are production-grade and serverless.
recommendation.mostReliable: AWS Lambda + API Gateway - robust, scalable, proven for Stripe webhooks.
recommendation.bestForSoloDev: Cloudflare Workers Free Tier - simple setup, no cold starts, global edge, and free up to 100k requests/day. Use raw Web Crypto for signature verification (sample code in Cloudflare docs).
recommendation.note: Stripe CLI + launchd is NOT recommended for production; only for local testing. ngrok is for testing only.
